await tools.progress.append_progress({content: `STAGE 2 — FINAL ANSWER (chosen design + rationale).
GOAL: commit to one hyperbolic metric that is distinct from the 4 already measured (Voronoi margin l1, adj_r2_l1, hsoftmax path, bucket_reach_lift_l1).
READ: the task brief only — no shell/filesystem available in this session, so the design is derived from the stated contract + the stated failure analysis of hyp_hsoftmax_path (collapse reward, -0.78 with level-2 bucket count).
OBSERVED / REASONING: all four prior metrics are either (a) local codebook-point geometry (Voronoi margin), (b) variance-decomposition (adj R2), (c) likelihood over the trie (path), or (d) a count-ratio lift. None measures WORST-CASE geometric coherence of a cell. Collapse beat the likelihood because a collapsed trie makes every path probable; a max/covering-radius functional is inverted in that respect — collapse makes the single cell's radius equal the whole cloud's radius, i.e. the worst possible score. So a normalized geodesic covering radius is intrinsically collapse-proof, which no prior metric was.
DESIGN: M = 1 - sum_b (n_b/N) * r_b / R, where r_b is the geodesic covering radius of level-1 cell b about its Frechet/Karcher barycentre in the curvature -1 Poincare ball, R the geodesic covering radius of the whole cloud about its own barycentre. Curvature enters three times: exp map of the reference vectors into the ball, the hyperbolic distance in the radii, and the Riemannian gradient for the barycentre.
DISTINCTNESS TO DECLARE: it is a max-over-items quantity (so bounded by geometry, not by counts), it is scale-normalized by R (so reference temperature/scale cancels), it is not a likelihood, not a variance ratio, not a margin, not a lift.
DEGENERACY CHECK: over-splitting is impossible at N=24587 with K1=256 (mean cell size ~96), and is anyway neutralized by the n_b/N weighting. Collapse scores 0. Worst plausible table = norm/radius-stratified hashing (thin radial shells), predicted to score low with a healthy bucket count.
OPEN: nothing; answer below stands on its own.

METRIC: hyp_frechet_cover_radius_l1
TITLE: Normalized geodesic covering radius of level-1 SID cells about their Poincare Frechet barycentres
FORMULA:
  Let N items, level-1 code c_i in {0..K1-1}, and z_i the frozen reference TARGET representation of item i.
  (1) Curve scale: tau = the Issue #126 reference's own temperature if recorded, else tau = 0.5*sqrt(mean_i ||z_i||^2) over the TRAINING split. No recall is read.
  (2) Exp map into the unit Poincare ball (curvature K = -1): x_i = tanh(||z_i||/(2*tau)) * z_i/||z_i||   (x_i = 0 if z_i = 0). So ||x_i|| < 1.
  (3) Hyperbolic distance: dH(x,y) = arcosh( 1 + 2||x-y||^2 / ((1-||x||^2)(1-||y||^2)) ).
  (4) Mobius ops, lambda_x = 2/(1-||x||^2):
      x (+) y = [ (1+2<x,y>+||y||^2)x + (1-||x||^2)y ] / ( 1 + 2<x,y> + ||x||^2||y||^2 )
      exp_x(v) = x (+) tanh(lambda_x*||v||/2) * v/||v||
      log_x(y) = (2/lambda_x) * artanh(lambda_x*||(-x)(+)y||) * ((-x)(+)y)/||(-x)(+)y||
  (5) For each code b with item set S_b, n_b = |S_b|:
      mu_b^(0) = (Euclidean mean of {x_i : i in S_b}) * 0.99 / max(1e-9, ||that mean||)  if ||mean|| >= 0.99, else the mean.
      Repeat T = 10 times (fixed, not tuned):
        mu_b^(t+1) = exp_{mu_b^(t)} ( (1/n_b) * sum_{i in S_b} log_{mu_b^(t)}(x_i) )
      mu_b = mu_b^(10).  r_b = max_{i in S_b} dH(mu_b, x_i)   (0 if n_b = 1).
  (6) Whole cloud: mu_all by the same recursion over all N items; R = max_i dH(mu_all, x_i).
  (7) METRIC: M = 1 - sum_{b=1..K1} (n_b/N) * (r_b / R).
  M in [0,1]; higher is better. Deterministic, one scalar, no fitted quantity.
INPUTS:
  - the exported Stage-2 SID table: item id -> integer level-1 code only (deeper levels are ignored);
  - the frozen Issue #126 behaviour reference: one target representation z_i per item (training-time artefact);
  - optionally the TRAINING split, only to compute tau when the reference records no temperature.
  Nothing else: no validation or test interaction, no recall, no Stage-3 output.
GEOMETRY:
  Fixed negative curvature K = -1, unit Poincare ball. Curvature enters at three points and cannot be removed: (a) the exp map at the origin with scale tau places each reference vector at hyperbolic radius artanh(||x_i||) * 2, so equal Euclidean steps near the boundary cost far more; (b) every radius is a Poincare geodesic length dH, not a chord; (c) each cell centre is a Frechet (Karcher) barycentre computed by Riemannian gradient descent using the exp/log maps, which has no closed Euclidean form. A Euclidean mean-and-radius version is NOT the same number: it would equalise cells that sit near the origin and near the boundary, which dH deliberately does not.
WHY IT SHOULD TRACK RECALL:
  Prefix retrieval returns the items sharing a level-1 prefix and then re-ranks them; so Recall@10 is governed by whether a cell is *uniformly* tight around its own centre, because a single straggler inside a cell can never be retrieved no matter how good the re-ranker is. A mean or a variance-explained score is dominated by the bulk and blind to that straggler; the covering radius is exactly the quantity the top-10 cut sees. The n_b/N weighting makes it an item-level statement ("the typical item's worst-case geodesic distance to its cell centre, relative to the whole cloud"), so it cannot be gamed by many empty-ish cells, and dividing by R removes the reference's overall spread and temperature, which is what makes tables from different Stage-2 configurations comparable. Over Q_H it adds: Q_H is an averaged prefix-ranking score that collapses at level 2 because the prefix becomes an item id, and it is unnormalised; this metric is a worst-case, scale-free, geometry-only statement that stays at level 1 and is therefore not contaminated by the level-2 degeneracy that killed Q_H at level 2/3 and killed the path likelihood outright.
COMPUTE:
  N = 24587, K1 = 256, d = reference dim. Barycentres: 10 Riemannian steps, each O(n_b * d) plus one exp/log pair per step => about 2 * 10 * N * d flops overall, i.e. ~10 * N * d, plus one N*N-free max per cell. With d = 256 this is ~6e7 flops: well under one second in numpy, under ten seconds in pure Python. Memory O(N*d) for the ball points plus O(N) codes. No pairwise item-item matrix is ever formed.
RISKS:
  (1) Degenerate if all level-1 codes are equal (R = r_b, M = 0) — but that table is genuinely the worst, so the value is informative rather than wrong.
  (2) Sensitive to a single outlier item: R is a max, so one far-out reference vector inflates R and pushes M toward 1 for every table, compressing the spread. Mitigation is not a tuned parameter but the option of taking R as the max over the training split only; this must be fixed a priori, not chosen by looking at the 97 recalls.
  (3) If the reference target vectors are strongly anisotropic (a few dominant directions), all cells look tight and M saturates high for every table, giving near-zero variance and near-zero correlation.
  (4) If level 1 is only the first token of a code whose semantics are carried by level 2, the metric reads the wrong partition.
  (5) If the reference is frozen but each run used a different reference feature space, the metric is comparing ball geometries of different point clouds; the contract assumes one frozen reference, so this must be checked before use.
FAILURE MODE:
  Worst on the SID table whose level-1 codes are assigned by radius/norm stratification — for example hashing on the reference norm, or a coarse k-means run on ||z_i|| alone. Such a table has a perfectly healthy bucket count (~96 items per code) and a healthy same-bucket ratio, but every cell is a thin radial shell spanning many angular sectors, so its geodesic covering radius is close to R and M is near 0, while recall is poor because direction, not norm, carries the neighbourhood. The mirror failure is a table that gets M = 0 by collapse: one code for all 24587 items. Both are exactly the cases where a count-based or likelihood-based metric is fooled, which is the point of the construction.
END METRIC`});

part.text:
METRIC: hyp_frechet_cover_radius_l1
TITLE: Normalized geodesic covering radius of level-1 SID cells about their Poincare Frechet barycentres
FORMULA:
  Let N items, level-1 code c_i in {0..K1-1}, and z_i the frozen reference TARGET representation of item i (in R^d).
  (1) Curve scale: tau = the Issue #126 reference's own temperature if recorded, else tau = 0.5*sqrt(mean_i ||z_i||^2) taken over the TRAINING split only. No recall is read.
  (2) Exp map into the unit Poincare ball (curvature K = -1): x_i = tanh(||z_i|| / (2*tau)) * z_i/||z_i||, and x_i = 0 if z_i = 0. Hence ||x_i|| < 1.
  (3) Hyperbolic distance: dH(x,y) = arcosh( 1 + 2||x-y||^2 / ((1-||x||^2)(1-||y||^2)) ).
  (4) Mobius ops with lambda_x = 2/(1-||x||^2):
      x (+) y = [ (1 + 2<x,y> + ||y||^2) x + (1 - ||x||^2) y ] / ( 1 + 2<x,y> + ||x||^2 ||y||^2 )
      exp_x(v) = x (+) tanh(lambda_x * ||v|| / 2) * v/||v||
      log_x(y) = (2/lambda_x) * artanh( lambda_x * ||(-x)(+)y|| ) * ((-x)(+)y) / ||(-x)(+)y||
  (5) For each code b with item set S_b, n_b = |S_b|:
      mu_b^(0) = Euclidean mean of {x_i : i in S_b}; if its norm >= 0.99, rescale it to norm 0.99.
      For t = 0..9 (T = 10, fixed, not tuned):
        mu_b^(t+1) = exp_{mu_b^(t)} ( (1/n_b) * sum_{i in S_b} log_{mu_b^(t)}(x_i) )
      mu_b = mu_b^(10);  r_b = max_{i in S_b} dH(mu_b, x_i),  with r_b = 0 when n_b = 1.
  (6) Whole cloud: mu_all by the same recursion over all N items; R = max_i dH(mu_all, x_i).
  (7) METRIC: M = 1 - sum_{b=1..K1} (n_b / N) * (r_b / R).
  M lies in [0,1], higher is better, one scalar, deterministic, nothing fitted.
INPUTS:
  - the exported Stage-2 SID table, using only the integer level-1 code per item (deeper levels are ignored);
  - the frozen Issue #126 behaviour reference, using only one target representation z_i per item;
  - optionally the TRAINING split, solely to compute tau when the reference records no temperature.
  Nothing else: no validation or test interaction, no recall, no Stage-3 output.
GEOMETRY:
  Fixed negative curvature K = -1 on the unit Poincare ball. Curvature enters at three points none of which can be removed: (a) the exp map at the origin with scale tau places z_i at hyperbolic radius 2*artanh(||x_i||), so equal Euclidean steps near the boundary cost far more than near the centre; (b) every radius is a Poincare geodesic length dH, not a chord; (c) each cell centre is a Frechet (Karcher) barycentre obtained by Riemannian gradient descent in the ball through exp/log maps, which has no closed Euclidean form. A Euclidean mean-and-radius substitute is a different number: it would treat a cell hugging the origin and a cell hugging the boundary as equally tight, which dH deliberately does not.
WHY IT SHOULD TRACK RECALL:
  Prefix retrieval returns the items sharing the level-1 prefix and re-ranks them, so Recall@10 is governed by whether a cell is uniformly tight about its own centre: a single straggler inside a cell can never be retrieved however strong the re-ranker is, yet a mean or a variance-explained score is dominated by the bulk and blind to exactly that item. The covering radius is the quantity the top-10 cut actually sees. Weighting by n_b/N makes the number an item-level statement, "the typical item's worst-case geodesic distance to its cell centre, relative to the whole cloud", so it cannot be gamed by many near-empty cells and so that the max is not carried by a single tiny code. Dividing by R removes the reference's overall spread and temperature, which is what makes tables from different Stage-2 configurations comparable at all. Over Q_H it adds: Q_H is an averaged prefix-ranking score that is unnormalised and collapses at level 2 because the prefix becomes nearly an item id (+0.634 at level 1, +0.287 at level 2); this metric is a worst-case, scale-free, geometry-only statement that stays at level 1 and never touches the level-2 degeneracy that also destroyed the path likelihood.
COMPUTE:
  N = 24587, K1 = 256, d at most 256. Barycentres need T*N exp/log pairs and about 2*T*N*d flops in total, plus one max per cell; with T = 10 that is ~1.3e8 elementary operations, i.e. well under a second in numpy and a few seconds in pure Python. Memory is O(N*d) for the ball points plus O(N) for the codes. No item-item matrix is ever formed, so the 24587^2 trap is avoided.
RISKS:
  (1) Degenerate when all level-1 codes coincide: then R = r_b and M = 0, which is the genuinely worst table, so the value stays informative rather than wrong.
  (2) R is a max, so one far-out reference vector inflates R and pushes every table's M toward 1, compressing the cross-run spread. The remedy is to fix R from the TRAINING split a priori, not to choose it by looking at the 97 recalls.
  (3) A strongly anisotropic reference makes all cells look tight and saturates M near 1 for every table, giving near-zero variance and no correlation.
  (4) If level 1 is uninformative and the semantic content lives only in level 2, the metric reads the wrong partition.
  (5) The construction assumes one frozen reference shared by every run; if runs used different reference feature spaces the ball geometries are not comparable and the metric must not be used across them.
FAILURE MODE:
  Worst on the SID table whose level-1 codes are assigned by radius or norm stratification, for example hashing on the reference norm or a coarse k-means run on ||z_i|| alone. Such a table has a perfectly healthy bucket count (about 96 items per code) and a healthy same-bucket ratio, but each cell is a thin radial shell spanning many angular sectors, so its geodesic covering radius is close to R and M is near 0 while recall is poor, because direction rather than norm carries the neighbourhood. The mirror failure is the fully collapsed table, one code for all 24587 items, which also gives M = 0. These are precisely the two tables on which count-based and likelihood-based metrics are fooled, which is the point of the construction.
END METRIC
